name: NE-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+27 district partisanship in a heavily Republican western Nebraska seat
Incumbent Adrian Smith running again with a large financial edge
Democratic challenger Becky Stille raised only $55k with minimal cash on hand
Prediction markets price Smith at roughly 96% to win
model.rationale: The district's R+27 lean, Smith's incumbency, and his roughly 30-to-1 fundraising advantage over Stille leave no credible path for a Democratic upset, and markets agree at about 96% Republican. The forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals-based margin with no evidence warranting movement.
model.watch: A major late outside spending push or an unexpected scandal involving Smith would be the only realistic way this moves toward competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Nebraska's 3rd District is one of the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+27. Adrian Smith has held it since 2007 and is running again with more than $1 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Becky Stille has raised about $55,000 and entered the fall with under $15,000 in cash. No outside groups are spending against Smith, and no independent or third-party candidates show meaningful financial support.

There are no public general-election polls and no expert raters flag the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets give Smith roughly a 96% chance of winning. The expected margin is about 21 points for Smith, consistent with the district's baseline adjusted slightly for the incumbent's financial edge. Any surprise would require an extraordinary external development.
